facts: Materials used for cryogenic disconnect seals (for example, Teflon/plastic spring-loaded seals) can become very brittle at low/cryogenic temperatures and can fracture, producing seal failure or reliability problems.

Widely different coefficients of thermal expansion lead to differential thermal contraction at cryogenic temperatures, causing large bolting problems, improper clearances or fits, loss of preload/alignment, and related seal/mating or hardware-interference issues.
payload.query: What two temperature-related material-selection concerns does NASA SP-8119 identify for cryogenic disconnects?
payload.answer:
Evidence-grounded answer:

- Materials used for cryogenic disconnect seals (for example, Teflon/plastic spring-loaded seals) can become very brittle at low/cryogenic temperatures and can fracture, producing seal failure or reliability problems. [nasa-sp-8119.pdf, pp. 65-66, chunk dd4b813f; nasa-sp-8119.pdf, pp. 130-132, chunk 5dac91e2]
- Widely different coefficients of thermal expansion lead to differential thermal contraction at cryogenic temperatures, causing large bolting problems, improper clearances or fits, loss of preload/alignment, and related seal/mating or hardware-interference issues. [nasa-sp-8119.pdf, pp. 85-88, chunk e689d758; nasa-sp-8119.pdf, pp. 130-132, chunk 5dac91e2]
